display.purpose: Game titles and the 404 headline; uppercase, condensed to 85%.

headline.purpose: Section heads such as the About title.

wordmark.purpose: Studio name in the top strip, with phosphor bloom.

control.purpose: Play button label; width inherited from body.

body.purpose: Hooks and About prose, always 400 at 100% width.

data.purpose: Base system voice: tagline, notes, footer.

label.purpose: Facts line and controls bar, uppercase tracked mono.

shadows.name: phosphor-bloom
shadows.purpose: Filter on wordmark and wombat glyph (10px on the large About glyph).

shadows.name: cursor-bloom
shadows.purpose: Filter on the selected cursor ship, in its row accent.

shadows.name: selected-lift
shadows.purpose: Neutral black lift under the selected, filled Play. Not a glow.

shadows.name: badge-lift
shadows.purpose: Legends of Loot unread badge, matching the game.

motion.name: row-field
motion.purpose: Row background fading to its field on selection.

motion.name: title-hook-color
motion.purpose: Title and hook colour change on selection.

motion.name: cursor
motion.purpose: Cursor ship sliding in from 10px left.

motion.name: play
motion.purpose: Play fill, colour and lift; arrow nudge 300ms.

motion.name: art-dim
motion.purpose: Unselected art dims to opacity 0.72 and saturate 0.7 on pointer devices.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All transitions collapse under prefers-reduced-motion; the canvas respects it too.

breakpoints.name: stack
breakpoints.purpose: Max-width: rows stack art-first at 5:2, every row lit, cursor and controls bar hidden, strip min-height 56px.

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Vector Game-Select Screen"**

The studio presents itself as the menu of an old vector-display arcade cabinet. A near-black, blue-tinted tube carries pale phosphor line ink: hairline rules, the wordmark, and a single-stroke wombat glyph that blooms slightly as real phosphor would. At rest a row shows its colour only on its Play outline and its own badge. Each game is a full-width menu row, and the selected row wakes up in that game's own palette: Legends of Loot in brown, gold and a red notification dot, Vector in cyan on a deep teal-black.

Density is low and deliberate. Two rows fill the first viewport, and each holds one big title, one hook, one line of facts and one Play control, with art on the right. Type does the arcade work: Tektur's squared, condensed display cuts for names and controls, and Martian Mono for everything that reads like data, hints or system text. The chrome stays flat and square. Colour, bloom and motion are reserved for the selection.
keyCharacteristics: Phosphor-on-black ground. Game colour fills a row only when it is selected, and Phosphor Cyan is the single house accent.
Full-width bands separated by 1px phosphor hairlines, with no cards.
Squared, uppercase Tektur display; Martian Mono for data, labels and keys.
Bloom only on line ink (wordmark, wombat glyph, cursor ship).
Selection is the signature interaction: arrow keys or pointer move a ship cursor, and the row's field, title and Play light up.

rules.name: The Lights-On Rule
rules.body: A game's colours stay on its own row. At rest the row carries its accent only on the Play outline and its own badge. Selection lights the field, title, hook and cursor (on narrow screens every row is lit). Shared chrome stays phosphor monochrome, with Phosphor Cyan as its only accent.

rules.name: The Own-Palette Rule
rules.body: Every game row declares its own accent and field. A new game brings its own colours from its own identity. It never borrows another game's colours or invents a studio accent.

rules.name: The Art-Scope Rule
rules.body: Colours inside game art (the Legends of Loot raster, and the Vector canvas's ship colours, amber gravity well and white tracers) belong to the art. They are not UI tokens.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Tektur speaks for names, controls and prose. Martian Mono speaks for data, hints, keys and system text. Never swap them.

rules.name: The Full-Width Prose Rule
rules.body: Running prose in Tektur is always weight 400 at 100% width. Only display sizes are condensed.

rules.name: The Real Subtitle Rule
rules.body: A tracked mono line under a title is used only when it is the game's actual subtitle. It is never a decorative label added above or below headings.

rules.name: The Phosphor-Only Glow Rule
rules.body: Coloured glow belongs only to stroked line ink: the wordmark, the wombat glyph and the cursor ship. Titles, prose and buttons never get coloured glow or text-shadow. Glow inside game art (the canvas's ships and gravity well) belongs to the art and is not a UI precedent.

dos: Do give every game row its own accent and field taken from that game's identity. At rest show the accent only on Play and the game's own badge, and light the field, title and hook on selection (always lit below 820px).
Do separate regions with 1px phosphor hairlines (rule) rather than cards, panels or background changes.
Do set titles in uppercase Tektur 800 at 85% width, and prose in Tektur 400 at 100% width.
Do use Martian Mono for facts, hints, keys, notes, the tagline and the footer.
Do keep chrome square, and round only the focus ring (2px), keycaps (3px) and the game's own badge (pill).
Do set each row's facts as one uppercase mono line, with items split by faint "/" separators.
donts: Don't put coloured glow or text-shadow on titles, prose or buttons. Bloom is for line ink only (wordmark, glyph, cursor).
Don't add any studio accent beyond Phosphor Cyan. Other colour belongs to the games, on their own rows.
Don't use ink-faint for text. It is for separators, borders and underlines only.
Don't lift Vector canvas colours (ship colours, amber well, white tracers) or Legends of Loot raster colours into UI chrome.
Don't add tracked mono labels above headings. A mono subtitle appears only when it is a game's real subtitle.
Don't use rounded cards or equal-card grids for games. Games are full-width menu rows.
